content.text:
No. The logic is reversed.

In `ci-impl.yml`:

```yaml
runs-on: ${{ !inputs.trusted && matrix.os || matrix.runner }}
```

For `trusted: false`, `!inputs.trusted` is true, so it selects `matrix.os` (`macos-latest` / `ubuntu-latest`)—GitHub-hosted runners.

The [linked job](https://github.com/jdx/fnox/actions/runs/34663183645/job/103470985317?pr=818) confirms this:

- Labels: `macos-latest`
- Runner group: `GitHub Actions`
- Runner: `GitHub Actions 1000754204`
- Startup banner: `Hosted Compute Agent`
- Namespace appears only in the matrix-generated job name

If untrusted builds should use Namespace, the expression should be:

```yaml
runs-on: ${{ inputs.trusted && matrix.os || matrix.runner }}
```

The Windows and final aggregation jobs remain GitHub-hosted regardless.
lol make a pr to fix that, also see if it's a problem on other jdx.dev clis

Yep—that inversion is real. I’ll fix fnox, then audit the other jdx.dev CLI repositories for the same trusted/untrusted runner expression and include only clearly equivalent fixes in a review-ready PR.
